On July 2, 2026, POSCO Holdings outlined a mid- to long-term portfolio transformation and financial strategy at its CEO Investor Day in Seoul. The group plans a “Triple-Core” portfolio built around Industrial, Strategic and Energy Resources, targeting overseas crude steel capacity of 10 million tons by 2031, lithium production of 173,000 tons by 2033 to rank among the top five global producers, and a broader footprint in rare earths, specialty gases, LNG and renewable energy. Management set 2028 financial goals of KRW 87.9 trillion in consolidated revenue and KRW 6.7 trillion in operating profit, supported by KRW 29.1 trillion in investment from 2026 to 2028. POSCO also announced a shareholder value-focused capital policy, aiming for a 35–40% payout of adjusted net income via dividends and buybacks, reducing holding-company discounts by monetizing some listed subsidiaries, and targeting a price-to-book ratio of at least 1.0x by 2028, signaling a bid to re-rate the stock and strengthen its strategic positioning in global resource markets. Valuation is also a headwind due to the high P/E, partially tempered by a moderate dividend yield. To see Spark’s full report on PKX stock, click here . More about POSCO POSCO Holdings Inc. is a South Korea-based industrial group rooted in steelmaking and increasingly focused on critical materials and energy. The company supplies crude steel globally, with expansion plans in high-growth markets such as India and the U.S., and is building positions in lithium, battery materials, rare earths, specialty gases, LNG and renewables to become a national supplier of critical resources.
